findingClass: a document fetch was REFUSED by the OD-37 network boundary (the hostname resolved to a private, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata address, or its address could not be resolved at all) and the refusal was not distinguishable from an ordinary transport failure in the logs
githubIssue: item 22 slice 3 (OD-37 / D17). `isResolvedAddressPrivate` shipped in #487 with ZERO callers, so the DNS-rebinding hole it was written to close stayed open on every exchange, SEBI and document rung. This slice wires it into the single `request()` choke point and gives the refusal its own outcome string.
failThreshold: any cycle in which a host that previously resolved public begins resolving private — i.e. an attempt whose outcome is `refused:resolved_private_address` for a host on the trusted allow-list. On a healthy cycle this count is ZERO: our own exchange and registrar hosts must never resolve inside the network. A non-zero count is either a real rebinding attempt or a DNS/resolver fault, and both need a human. `reason: resolver_error` is counted separately from `reason: resolved_private_address`, because the first is fail-closed behaviour on a broken resolver and the second is the attack this exists to stop; collapsing them would hide a rebinding attempt inside a DNS outage.
unverifiableWhen: ENABLE_RESOLVED_ADDRESS_REFUSAL is OFF for the slot being read — the check then evaluates nothing, and MUST report UNVERIFIABLE rather than PASS. A zero refusal count from a slot where the refusal is switched off is not evidence that no host resolved private; it is evidence that nothing looked. (This run has produced four separate defects of exactly that shape today, including a staging proof that would have measured a disabled feature.)
notCoveredReason: There is no `record('document_download_refusals'` call in scripts/audit-detection-floor.mjs yet, so this is a DESIGN-TIME check, not a live one. Per .claude/rules/recurrence-detection-gate.md it stays in notCoveredByThisManifest until that call lands — listing it under `checks` before the audit implements it would be a paper check, would fail scripts/tests/audit-detection-floor.test.mjs case 79, and would read as wider coverage than the floor actually has. What EXISTS today is the per-refusal log line (`OD-37 download refusal: ...`, carrying host, url, ipoKey and reason) plus the `refused:resolved_private_address` attempt outcome; what is MISSING is a nightly consumer that counts them and diffs against the previous run.
